info.title: Rookery API
info.description: Virtual-machine, storage, network, and VPP management API.

delete.summary:
DetachHostInterface removes the VPP host-interface; the Linux NIC becomes
available to the host again.

post.summary:
AttachHostInterface takes over a host NIC into VPP and persists it so it
is recreated after a VPP restart.

get.summary:
ListHostTaps lists persistent taps that connect a Rookery Network to the
Linux host.

post.summary:
CreateHostTap creates a VPP tap on a network bridge domain and persists it
so it is recreated after an API or VPP restart.

delete.summary: DeleteHostTap removes a persistent network host tap.

get.summary:
ListInterfaceCounters returns cumulative VPP RX/TX counters for every
registered virtual interface. It must be declared after GetInterface:
grpc-gateway registers handlers in declaration order and tries the newest
first, so the literal /api/interfaces/counters path must be registered
after the /api/interfaces/{id} pattern to win over it.

delete.summary:
ResetInterfaceCounters clears the RX/TX counters for all VPP interfaces
(vppctl clear interfaces). Like ListInterfaceCounters it must stay after
DeleteInterface so the literal path beats /api/interfaces/{id}.

get.summary:
GetVPPInterfaceAddresses returns Rookery-managed IPv4/IPv6 addresses for a
VPP interface owned by Rookery (vhost-user, host tap, host interface, or
VNF tap).

GetVPPInterfaceRouteTables returns the IPv4/IPv6 FIB binding for a Rookery
host interface, host tap, or bridge-domain pipe endpoint. Vhost-user
interfaces use the dedicated /api/interfaces/{id}/route-tables endpoint.

delete.summary:
DeleteVPPInterfaceRouteTables removes an explicit route-table override so
the interface returns to its automatic default (the network VRF for host
taps, or the default table for host interfaces).

replace_interface_ids.description:
Explicit replacement lets clients clear the interface set. Disks cannot
be cleared because every VM requires at least one disk.

protobufNullValue.description:
`NullValue` is a singleton enumeration to represent the null value for the
`Value` type union.

 The JSON representation for `NullValue` is JSON `null`.

 - NULL_VALUE: Null value.

v1DHCPOption.description:
DHCPOption is an extra DHCPv4/DHCPv6 option advertised by a DHCP VNF.
Format selects how Value is encoded: string, ipv4, ipv6, hex, uint8, uint16,
uint32, or domain-list. Server-managed option codes are rejected.

v1DNSRecord.description:
DNSRecord is one local record served by a DNS VNF. Name is a fully qualified
domain name; wildcard names such as *.lab1.test are supported. Type is A,
AAAA, CNAME, TXT, or PTR.

v1HostTap.description:
HostTap is a VPP tap that bridges a Rookery Network to the Linux host. The
host-side interface is named `name`; `ipv4_address` is optional and, when
set, is assigned to that interface.

transport.description:
Transport override for DHCPv4: shared, dedicated, or tap. memif is a
legacy alias for dedicated memif. Empty selects the network default.
BGP supports tap and memif (dedicated) transport.

next_hop.description:
next_hop overrides the BGP NEXT_HOP for advertised prefixes. Empty means
use local_ip. Must match the local_ip address family.

dns_records.description:
DNS configuration. Records are served authoritatively; names without a
local record are forwarded when dns_forward is enabled. If dns_forward is
enabled and dns_forwarders is empty, the daemon uses the host resolver
configuration (/etc/resolv.conf).

dhcp_options.description:
Extra DHCPv4/DHCPv6 options advertised by a DHCP VNF. DNS (v4 option 6,
v6 option 23) and server-managed options are rejected; use config.dns for
DNS servers.

dns_vnf_id.description:
DHCP DNS integration. Select a DNS VNF on the same network; the daemon
creates dynamic A/AAAA and PTR records for active DHCP leases. DNSDomain
is the suffix used when a client does not provide an FQDN; DNSTTL is the
dynamic record TTL in seconds (0 means the default 300).
